title: Forklift operator training and evaluation practice questions
description: Practice questions on OSHA forklift operator training rules: who trains, training content, refresher training, evaluation and certification (29 CFR 1910.178(l)).

questions.topic: Safe operation and who may operate
questions.question: An employer is writing the opening line of its forklift operator training policy and wants it to match the overall duty in 1910.178(l)(1)(i). Which duty is that?

options.A: Ensure that each operator passes a test given by OSHA
options.B: Ensure that each operator is competent to operate a truck safely, as shown by successful completion of the training and evaluation in paragraph (l)
options.C: Ensure that each operator has logged a set number of hours on a truck
options.D: Ensure that each operator signs a statement that he or she can drive a truck safely

questions.explanation: The employer "shall ensure that each powered industrial truck operator is competent to operate a powered industrial truck safely, as demonstrated by the successful completion of the training and evaluation specified in this paragraph (l)."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1910.178, Powered industrial trucks (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.topic: Safe operation and who may operate
questions.question: 1910.178(l)(1)(ii) bars an employer from permitting an employee who has not completed the required training to operate a truck. For what purpose does that sentence allow operation anyway, apart from what (l)(5) permits?

options.A: Short trips of under 100 feet
options.B: Overtime shifts
options.C: Emergencies when no trained operator is present
options.D: Training purposes

questions.explanation: The rule applies "Prior to permitting an employee to operate a powered industrial truck (except for training purposes)" and also notes "except as permitted by paragraph (l)(5)."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1910.178, Powered industrial trucks (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.question: A trainee is driving under the direct supervision of a qualified trainer. What other condition does 1910.178(l)(2)(i) set for the trainee's operation?

options.A: The operation does not endanger the trainee or other employees
options.B: The truck carries no load at any time
options.C: The trainee drives only outside working hours
options.D: The trainee drives only on public roads

questions.explanation: Trainees may operate a truck only under direct supervision "and" only "Where such operation does not endanger the trainee or other employees."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1910.178, Powered industrial trucks (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.question: A training program has lectures, a video and written material, followed by an evaluation of each operator's performance in the workplace. It includes no demonstrations performed by the trainer and no practical exercises performed by the trainee. Under 1910.178(l)(2)(ii), which element of training is missing?

options.A: Nothing, because formal instruction and evaluation are enough
options.B: A medical examination of the trainee
options.C: Practical training
options.D: A written test approved by the truck's manufacturer

questions.explanation: Training "shall consist of a combination of formal instruction", "practical training (demonstrations performed by the trainer and practical exercises performed by the trainee), and evaluation of the operator's performance in the workplace."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1910.178, Powered industrial trucks (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.question: 1910.178(l)(2)(ii) gives examples of each training element. Which of these does it list as an example of formal instruction?

options.A: Practical exercises performed by the trainee
options.B: Interactive computer learning
options.C: Demonstrations performed by the trainer
options.D: Evaluation of the operator's performance in the workplace

questions.explanation: The rule lists "formal instruction (e.g., lecture, discussion, interactive computer learning, video tape, written material)"; demonstrations by the trainer and exercises by the trainee are "practical training".

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1910.178, Powered industrial trucks (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.question: An employer's only check on its operators is a written quiz taken in a break room. Under 1910.178(l)(2)(ii), the evaluation that forms part of training is an evaluation of what?

options.A: The operator's score on a written quiz
options.B: The operator's driving record on public roads
options.C: The operator's years of service with the employer
options.D: The operator's performance in the workplace

questions.explanation: The third element of training under (l)(2)(ii) is "evaluation of the operator's performance in the workplace."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1910.178, Powered industrial trucks (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.question: Under 1910.178(l)(3), in which listed topics may initial training be left out?

options.A: Topics the operator would prefer to skip
options.B: Topics that take more than one hour to teach
options.C: Topics which the employer can demonstrate are not applicable to safe operation of the truck in the employer's workplace
options.D: Topics the trainer has not taught before

questions.explanation: Operators "shall receive initial training in the following topics, except in topics which the employer can demonstrate are not applicable to safe operation of the truck in the employer's workplace."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1910.178, Powered industrial trucks (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.question: Which of these is listed in 1910.178(l)(3)(i) as a truck-related training topic?

options.A: Differences between the truck and the automobile
options.B: How to apply for a commercial driver's license
options.C: The history of the truck's manufacturer
options.D: Resale values of used trucks

questions.explanation: The truck-related topics include "Differences between the truck and the automobile".

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1910.178, Powered industrial trucks (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.question: Which vehicle inspection and maintenance does 1910.178(l)(3)(i)(J) list as a training topic?

options.A: Every procedure in the manufacturer's service manual
options.B: Only maintenance done by outside mechanics
options.C: Only the annual inspection done by the dealer
options.D: Any vehicle inspection and maintenance that the operator will be required to perform

questions.explanation: The topic is "Any vehicle inspection and maintenance that the operator will be required to perform".

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1910.178, Powered industrial trucks (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.question: 1910.178(l)(3)(i)(M) adds any other operating instructions, warnings, or precautions found where?

options.A: In the local fire code
options.B: In the operator's manual for the types of vehicle that the employee is being trained to operate
options.C: In the truck dealer's sales brochure
options.D: In a highway driving handbook

questions.explanation: The topic covers "Any other operating instructions, warnings, or precautions listed in the operator's manual for the types of vehicle that the employee is being trained to operate."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1910.178, Powered industrial trucks (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.topic: Initial training: workplace topics and the section's requirements
questions.question: 1910.178(l)(3)(ii)(G) lists ramps and other sloped surfaces as a workplace-related topic. What does it say such surfaces could affect?

options.A: The vehicle's stability
options.B: The operator's hearing
options.C: The building's insurance rating
options.D: The truck's paint finish

questions.explanation: The topic is "Ramps and other sloped surfaces that could affect the vehicle's stability".

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1910.178, Powered industrial trucks (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.topic: Initial training: workplace topics and the section's requirements
questions.question: Operators at a plant will drive through a room that has been classified as a hazardous location. How does 1910.178(l)(3) treat that room in initial training?

options.A: It is left out, because truck designations alone deal with hazardous locations
options.B: It is covered only in refresher training, not in initial training
options.C: Hazardous (classified) locations where the vehicle will be operated are a workplace-related training topic
options.D: It is covered only if the operator asks for it

questions.explanation: The workplace-related topics in (l)(3)(ii) include "Hazardous (classified) locations where the vehicle will be operated".

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1910.178, Powered industrial trucks (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.question: Under 1910.178(l)(4)(i), what must refresher training include?

options.A: A new driver's license check
options.B: A medical examination of the operator
options.C: A written test from the truck manufacturer
options.D: An evaluation of the effectiveness of that training

questions.explanation: "Refresher training, including an evaluation of the effectiveness of that training, shall be conducted as required by paragraph (l)(4)(ii)".

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1910.178, Powered industrial trucks (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.question: No accident has happened, but an operator's evaluation reveals that the operator is not operating the truck safely. What does 1910.178(l)(4)(ii) require?

options.A: Refresher training in relevant topics shall be provided to the operator
options.B: Nothing until the operator is involved in an accident
options.C: Only a written warning placed in the operator's file
options.D: Only that the evaluation be sent to OSHA

questions.explanation: "Refresher training in relevant topics shall be provided to the operator when" (among other situations) "The operator has received an evaluation that reveals that the operator is not operating the truck safely".

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1910.178, Powered industrial trucks (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.question: In which topics does 1910.178(l)(4)(ii) require refresher training to be provided?

options.A: Only the workplace-related topics
options.B: Relevant topics
options.C: Only topics the operator chooses
options.D: Only topics covered in the operator's manual

questions.explanation: The rule states: "Refresher training in relevant topics shall be provided to the operator when" one of the listed situations occurs.

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1910.178, Powered industrial trucks (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.question: An employer installs new racking that narrows the aisles where its trucks run. Under 1910.178(l)(4)(ii), what follows?

options.A: Nothing, because the trucks themselves did not change
options.B: Only a new nameplate on each truck
options.C: Refresher training in relevant topics, because a condition in the workplace changed in a manner that could affect safe operation of the truck
options.D: Only a memo to operators

questions.explanation: Refresher training in relevant topics shall be provided when "A condition in the workplace changes in a manner that could affect safe operation of the truck."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1910.178, Powered industrial trucks (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.question: What does 1910.178(l)(8) say Appendix A to the section provides?

options.A: Mandatory training hours for each type of truck
options.B: A required written test for operators
options.C: Additional requirements that replace paragraph (l)
options.D: Non-mandatory guidance to assist employers in implementing paragraph (l)

questions.explanation: "Appendix A to this section provides non-mandatory guidance to assist employers in implementing this paragraph (l). This appendix does not add to, alter, or reduce the requirements of this section."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1910.178, Powered industrial trucks (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.question: An operator who moved from another employer was trained there in vehicle stability. The new employer finds that this training is not appropriate to the truck and working conditions at its plant. Does 1910.178(l)(5) excuse additional training in that topic?

options.A: No; (l)(5) applies only where the earlier training is appropriate to the truck and working conditions encountered
options.B: Yes, because any earlier training in a listed topic counts
options.C: Yes, if the earlier training took place within the past three years
options.D: Yes, if the operator signs a statement that the earlier training covered the topic

questions.explanation: Paragraph (l)(5) applies only where the operator "has previously received training in a topic specified in paragraph (l)(3) of this section, and such training is appropriate to the truck and working conditions encountered", and then only "if the operator has been evaluated and found competent to operate the truck safely."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1910.178, Powered industrial trucks (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.question: 1910.178(l)(3)(i)(A) lists operating instructions, warnings, and precautions as a truck-related topic. For which trucks?

options.A: Every type of truck the employer owns
options.B: Every type of truck sold in the United States
options.C: The types of truck the operator will be authorized to operate
options.D: Only the truck used for the trainee's practical exercises

questions.explanation: The topic is "Operating instructions, warnings, and precautions for the types of truck the operator will be authorized to operate".

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1910.178, Powered industrial trucks (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.question: Which restrictions does 1910.178(l)(3)(i)(F) name in its visibility training topic?

options.A: Restrictions due to building lighting
options.B: Restrictions due to loading
options.C: Restrictions due to tinted windows
options.D: Restrictions due to the operator's eyesight

questions.explanation: The truck-related topic is "Visibility (including restrictions due to loading)".
